t.en: Compute sums and differences of vectors algebraically and geometrically.
Use the laws of vector addition to prove equalities between vector expressions.
Addition of vectors in $\R^n$ is defined as follows.

For vectors $\vect{u}=\left[\begin{array}{c} u_1 \\ \vdots \\ u_n \end{array}\right],\; \vect{v}= \left[\begin{array}{c} v_1 \\ \vdots \\ v_n \end{array}\right] \in \R^n$, the sum $\vect{u}+\vect{v}\in \R^n$ is defined by

blocks.tex:
\vect{u}+\vect{v} = \left[\begin{array}{c}
      u_1 \\
      \vdots \\
      u_n
    \end{array}\right] +  \left[\begin{array}{c}
      v_1 \\
      \vdots \\
      v_n
    \end{array}\right]
    = \left[\begin{array}{c}
      u_1+v_1 \\
      \vdots \\
      u_n+v_n
    \end{array}\right].

t.en: To add vectors, we simply add corresponding components. Therefore, in order to add vectors, they must be the same size. For example, $\mat{1, 2, 3}^T + \mat{4, 5, 6}^T = \mat{1+4, 2+5, 3+6}^T = \mat{5, 7, 9}^T$.
The geometric significance of vector addition in $\R^n$ is given in the following proposition.

Let $\vect{u}$ and $\vect{v}$ be two vectors in $\R^n$. Slide $\vect{v}$ so that the tail of $\vect{v}$ is on the tip of $\vect{u}$. Then draw the arrow which goes from the tail of $\vect{u}$ to the tip of $\vect{v}$. This arrow represents the vector $\vect{u}+\vect{v}$.
Let $\vect{u}$ and $\vect{v}$ be two vectors. Using the geometry of vector addition, explain why $\vect{u}+\vect{v} = \vect{v} + \vect{u}$.

In the following diagram, the vectors $\vect{u}$ and $\vect{v}$ form a parallelogram. Therefore, whether we line up the tail of $\vect{u}$ with the tip of $\vect{v}$ or vice versa, we obtain the same vector, which is both $\vect{u}+\vect{v}$ and $\vect{v}+\vect{u}$.

The **negative** of a vector $\vect{u}=\left[\begin{array}{c} u_1 \\ \vdots \\ u_n \end{array}\right]\in\R^n$ is defined by $-\vect{u} = \left[\begin{array}{c} -u_1 \\ \vdots \\ -u_n \end{array}\right]$.
Geometrically, the vector $-\vect{u}$ has the same magnitude as $\vect{u}$, but the opposite direction.

To define the **subtraction** of two vectors, we simply regard $\vect{u}-\vect{v}$ as an abbreviation for $\vect{u} + (-\vect{v})$, exactly as we do with real numbers. Algebraically, this just amounts to componentwise subtraction:

blocks.tex:
\left[\begin{array}{c}
    u_1 \\
    \vdots \\
    u_n
  \end{array}\right] - \left[\begin{array}{c}
    v_1 \\
    \vdots \\
    v_n
  \end{array}\right]
  = \left[\begin{array}{c}
    u_1-v_1 \\
    \vdots \\
    u_n-v_n
  \end{array}\right].

Addition of vectors satisfies some important properties which are outlined in the following proposition. Recall that $\vect{0}$ is the **zero vector**, the vector from $\R^n$ in which all components are equal to $0$.
The following properties hold for vectors $\vect{u},\vect{v},\vect{w}\in\R^n$.
The commutative law of addition
The associative law of addition
The existence of an additive unit
The existence of an additive inverse
Find $\left[\begin{array}{c} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{array}\right] + \left[\begin{array}{c} 1 \\ 5 \\ 1 \end{array}\right] + \left[\begin{array}{c} -1 \\ 2 \\ -4 \end{array}\right]$.
$\left[\begin{array}{r} 1 \\ 9 \\ 0 \end{array}\right]$.

t.en: Use the properties of vector addition from Proposition “Properties of vector addition” to show the following equalities. Justify every step.
$(\vect{u}+\vect{v})+\vect{w} = (\vect{v}+\vect{w})+\vect{u}$.
$(\vect{u}+\vect{0})+(\vect{v}+(-\vect{u})) = \vect{v}$.

$(\vect{u}+\vect{v})+\vect{w} = (\vect{v}+\vect{u})+\vect{w} = \vect{v}+(\vect{u}+\vect{w}) = \vect{v}+(\vect{w}+\vect{u}) = (\vect{v}+\vect{w})+\vect{u}$. Here we have used the commutative law, the associative law, the commutative law, and the associative law, in that order.

$(\vect{u}+\vect{0})+(\vect{v}+(-\vect{u})) = \vect{u}+(\vect{v}+(-\vect{u})) = \vect{u}+((-\vect{u})+\vect{v}) = (\vect{u}+(-\vect{u}))+\vect{v} = \vect{0}+\vect{v} = \vect{v}+\vect{0} = \vect{v}$. Here we have used the additive unit, the commutative law, the associative law, the additive inverse, the commutative law, and the additive unit, in that order.
